chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa who said:

Ibrahim ibn Uqbah wrote to him asking about Fitrah (alms of fasting), how much is it, in the weight of Baghdad, for every head? And is it permissible to give it to a non-believer? So he wrote to him: You must give from yourself one Sa' (measure) in the Sa' of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and from your dependents also, and it is not appropriate that you give your Zakat except to a believer.

key_terms.رِطْلُ بَغْدَادَ: Ratl of Baghdad (a specific unit of weight)

ai.seo_question: How much is the Fitrah payment and who is eligible to receive it according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani establishes the standard measure for Fitrah as one Sa' per individual, aligning with the Prophetic tradition, while explicitly restricting its distribution to believers (Mu'minun). This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between Fitrah and general Zakat, emphasizing the spiritual purity of the recipient in this specific act of worship. The restriction to believers underscores the concept of 'Wilayah' and the preferential status of the faithful in receiving religious dues.
